claim: Leishmania donovani causes visceral leishmaniasis (VL), the second most deadly vector-borne parasitic disease.
source: Leishmania donovani causes visceral leishmaniasis (VL), the second most deadly vector-borne parasitic disease.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that establishes the disease context.

claim: A recent epidemic in the Indian subcontinent (ISC) caused up to 80% of global VL and over 30,000 deaths per year.
source: A recent epidemic in the Indian subcontinent (ISC) caused up to 80% of global VL and over 30,000 deaths per year.
evidence: This statement provides epidemiological data about the burden of VL in the ISC.

claim: Resistance against antimonial drugs has probably been a contributing factor in the persistence of this epidemic.
source: Resistance against antimonial drugs has probably been a contributing factor in the persistence of this epidemic.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the role of drug resistance in the epidemic.

claim: 204 clinical isolates were used to track the evolution and epidemiology of L. donovani from the ISC.
source: Here we use whole genome sequences from 204 clinical isolates to track the evolution and epidemiology of L. donovani from the ISC.
evidence: This describes the sample size and approach of the study.

claim: Independent radiations have emerged since a bottleneck coincident with 1960s DDT spraying campaigns.
source: We identify independent radiations that have emerged since a bottleneck coincident with 1960s DDT spraying campaigns.
evidence: This is a finding from the phylogenetic analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: A genetically distinct population frequently resistant to antimonials has a two base-pair insertion in the aquaglyceroporin gene LdAQP1 that prevents the transport of trivalent antimonials.
source: A genetically distinct population frequently resistant to antimonials has a two base-pair insertion in the aquaglyceroporin gene LdAQP1 that prevents the transport of trivalent antimonials.
evidence: This is a key finding linking a genetic variant to drug resistance.

claim: There is evidence of genetic exchange between ISC populations.
source: We find evidence of genetic exchange between ISC populations, and show that the mutation in LdAQP1 has spread by recombination.
evidence: This describes evidence for recombination between populations.

claim: The mutation in LdAQP1 has spread by recombination.
source: We find evidence of genetic exchange between ISC populations, and show that the mutation in LdAQP1 has spread by recombination.
evidence: This describes the mechanism by which the resistance mutation has spread.

claim: There are probably between 200,000 and 300,000 VL cases annually.
source: There are probably between 200,000 and 300,000 VL cases annually (Alvar et al., 2012), leading to as many as 50,000 deaths per year (den Boer et al., 2011; Lozano et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a cited estimate of global VL burden.

claim: VL leads to as many as 50,000 deaths per year.
source: There are probably between 200,000 and 300,000 VL cases annually (Alvar et al., 2012), leading to as many as 50,000 deaths per year (den Boer et al., 2011; Lozano et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a cited estimate of VL mortality.

claim: As much as 80% of the global VL burden occurs in the Indian sub-continent.
source: VL is widespread in both the New and Old Worlds (Pigott et al., 2014), but as much as 80% of the global VL burden occurs in the Indian sub-continent (Alvar et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a cited statistic about the geographic distribution of VL.

claim: Recent intensified control efforts have led to a notable decline in cases.
source: Recent intensified control efforts have led to a notable decline in cases (Chowdhury et al., 2014) but the problem is not yet eliminated.
evidence: This is a cited observation about recent trends in VL incidence.

claim: VL was first reported in the Indian sub-continent (ISC) in the 1820s.
source: VL was first reported in the Indian sub-continent (ISC) in the 1820s, but initially confused with malaria until the discovery of L. donovani in 1903 (Gibson, 1983).
evidence: This is a historical fact cited from the literature.

claim: VL was nearly eliminated from the ISC in the 1960s by antimalarial spraying campaigns with DDT.
source: Although VL was nearly eliminated from the ISC in the 1960s (Thakur, 2007) by antimalarial spraying campaigns with DDT, it re-emerged in 1977 and has caused several subsequent major epidemics (Dye and Wolpert, 1988).
evidence: This is a cited historical observation about VL control.

claim: VL re-emerged in 1977 and has caused several subsequent major epidemics.
source: Although VL was nearly eliminated from the ISC in the 1960s (Thakur, 2007) by antimalarial spraying campaigns with DDT, it re-emerged in 1977 and has caused several subsequent major epidemics (Dye and Wolpert, 1988).
evidence: This is a cited historical observation about VL epidemiology.

claim: The parasite developed resistance to both SbIII and SbV.
source: The parasite developed resistance to both SbIII and SbV, and after ten years of clinical use there has been a notable decline in MIL efficacy (Rijal et al., 2013; 2007; Sundar et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a cited observation about drug resistance development.

claim: After ten years of clinical use there has been a notable decline in MIL efficacy.
source: The parasite developed resistance to both SbIII and SbV, and after ten years of clinical use there has been a notable decline in MIL efficacy (Rijal et al., 2013; 2007; Sundar et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a cited observation about miltefosine resistance.

claim: Leishmania parasites can re-shape their genome rapidly in vitro in response to stress.
source: Leishmania parasites can re-shape their genome rapidly in vitro in response to stress (Leprohon et al., 2009), suggesting structural variation is an important feature by which they can rapidly adapt to changing environmental conditions and drug pressure.
evidence: This is a cited observation about Leishmania genome plasticity.

claim: Structural variation is an important feature by which Leishmania can rapidly adapt to changing environmental conditions and drug pressure.
source: Leishmania parasites can re-shape their genome rapidly in vitro in response to stress (Leprohon et al., 2009), suggesting structural variation is an important feature by which they can rapidly adapt to changing environmental conditions and drug pressure.
evidence: This is an inference based on cited observations.

claim: L. donovani within the ISC show very little genetic differentiation based on existing genetic markers.
source: While an extensive literature has made use of molecular methods to study the population genetics of Leishmania (e.g. Alam et al., 2009; Lukes et al., 2007; Mauricio et al., 2006; Schonian et al., 2008), existing genetic markers have relatively poor resolution, and in particular L. donovani within the ISC show very little genetic differentiation based on these approaches (Alam et al., 2009; Downing et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a cited observation about the limitations of previous genetic studies.

claim: Whole-genome sequence data has the potential to show significant population structure within the ISC.
source: Whole-genome sequence data has the potential to show significant population structure within the ISC, and also allows us to identify changes in genome structure.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential of the genomic approach used in this study.

claim: 204 L. donovani isolates were obtained from VL patients between 2002 and 2011 from regions in Nepal (N=98), India (N=98) and Bangladesh (N=8).
source: Here we report the genome sequences of 204 L. donovani isolates (Figure 1, Supplementary file 1), obtained from VL patients between 2002 and 2011 from regions in Nepal (N=98), India (N=98) and Bangladesh (N=8) that represent the epicentre of the on-going VL epidemic in the ISC (Figure 1a).
evidence: This describes the sample collection for the study.

claim: Three divergent genetic lineages are circulating in the ISC region.
source: Calling variants against a reference genome assembly for a Nepalese L. donovani strain (BPK282/0cl4; Figure 2—figure supplement 1), we identify three divergent genetic lineages circulating in this region (Figure 2b): a core group of 191 closely related parasites found in the highly endemic lowlands of all three countries, a small population of 12 Nepalese isolates found most frequently in the highlands (ISC1) and a single divergent Nepalese isolate (BPK512/0cl9) (Downing et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a finding from the phylogenetic analysis.

claim: The two main groups show fixed differences at 45,743 sites.
source: These two main groups show fixed differences at 45,743 sites (Supplementary file 2, table a), and two previously sequenced Sri Lankan L. donovani isolates (Zhang et al., 2014) were more closely related to the core population (21,546 fixed differences) than to ISC1 (45,743 fixed differences).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the genetic analysis.

claim: Two previously sequenced Sri Lankan L. donovani isolates were more closely related to the core population than to ISC1.
source: These two main groups show fixed differences at 45,743 sites (Supplementary file 2, table a), and two previously sequenced Sri Lankan L. donovani isolates (Zhang et al., 2014) were more closely related to the core population (21,546 fixed differences) than to ISC1 (45,743 fixed differences).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing the ISC isolates to published genomes.

claim: Parasites within each group show little SNP variation with only 5,628 variable sites in ISC1 and just 2,418 sites varying within the core population.
source: Parasites within each group show little SNP variation with only 5,628 variable sites in ISC1 and just 2,418 sites varying within the core population (Supplementary file 2, table b) and correspondingly few SNPs in protein-coding regions (Supplementary file 2, table c).
evidence: This is a quantitative result describing genetic diversity within populations.

claim: Core population isolates differ at an average of 88.3 nucleotide sites with an average nucleotide diversity of 9.7 per Mb.
source: Core population isolates differ at an average of 88.3 nucleotide sites with an average nucleotide diversity of 9.7 per Mb (Supplementary file 2, table d).
evidence: This is a quantitative measure of genetic diversity.

claim: A panel of microsatellite markers shows no variation between isolates from the core population.
source: While a panel of microsatellite markers shows no variation between isolates from the core population (Downing et al., 2012), we reveal significant spatial and temporal genetic structure within this group despite this extremely low level of overall diversity (Figure 2a,c; Supplementary file 2, table e).
evidence: This is a cited observation contrasting previous methods with the current genomic approach.

claim: Significant spatial and temporal genetic structure exists within the core population despite extremely low overall diversity.
source: While a panel of microsatellite markers shows no variation between isolates from the core population (Downing et al., 2012), we reveal significant spatial and temporal genetic structure within this group despite this extremely low level of overall diversity (Figure 2a,c; Supplementary file 2, table e).
evidence: This is a key finding showing the power of genomic data to detect population structure.

claim: Phylogenetic and clustering methods identify six congruent monophyletic groups (ISC2-7).
source: Phylogenetic and clustering methods identify six congruent monophyletic groups (ISC2-7).
evidence: This describes the population structure identified in the study.

claim: Three other groups (ISC8-10) and 21 ungrouped isolates had more complex and less certain evolutionary histories.
source: Three other groups (ISC8-10) and 21 ungrouped isolates had more complex and less certain evolutionary histories (Figure 2a,c; Supplementary file 2, table f).
evidence: This describes isolates with uncertain population assignment.

claim: Most of the ISC groups are present throughout the sampling window (2002–2011), and many are present in both India and Nepal.
source: Most of the ISC groups are present throughout our sampling window (2002–2011), and many are present in both India and Nepal (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the temporal and spatial distribution of the identified populations.

claim: ISC7 represents a recent radiation first observed in 2006 with almost no diversity and is restricted to India.
source: There are some exceptions: ISC7 represents a recent radiation (first observed in 2006) with almost no diversity (20 unique SNPs; Supplementary file 2, table g; π=1.8 per Mb) and is restricted to India, while ISC6 is an older and more diverse group restricted to Nepal (π=12.2 per Mb).
evidence: This describes the characteristics of a specific population.

claim: ISC6 is an older and more diverse group restricted to Nepal.
source: There are some exceptions: ISC7 represents a recent radiation (first observed in 2006) with almost no diversity (20 unique SNPs; Supplementary file 2, table g; π=1.8 per Mb) and is restricted to India, while ISC6 is an older and more diverse group restricted to Nepal (π=12.2 per Mb).
evidence: This describes the characteristics of a specific population.

claim: ISC5 is distinguished from other groups by just 32 SNP sites.
source: We observe subsequent evolution within some groups: ISC5 is distinguished from other groups by just 32 SNP sites (Supplementary file 2, table h), but contains a subgroup with multiple novel SNPs and lower somy (Supplementary file 2, table i).
evidence: This describes the genetic characteristics of ISC5.

claim: ISC5 contains a subgroup with multiple novel SNPs and lower somy.
source: We observe subsequent evolution within some groups: ISC5 is distinguished from other groups by just 32 SNP sites (Supplementary file 2, table h), but contains a subgroup with multiple novel SNPs and lower somy (Supplementary file 2, table i).
evidence: This describes internal structure within ISC5.

claim: The core population diverged in the mid 19th century.
source: Bayesian phylogenetic models in an explicit temporal and spatial framework revealed that the core population diverged in the mid 19th century (Figure 1b), matching the dates of the earliest reports of large-scale VL outbreaks in the ISC (Gibson, 1983) and thus suggesting that modern lowland parasites descend from these early epidemics.
evidence: This is a result from the Bayesian phylogenetic dating analysis.

claim: Modern lowland parasites descend from early 19th century epidemics.
source: Bayesian phylogenetic models in an explicit temporal and spatial framework revealed that the core population diverged in the mid 19th century (Figure 1b), matching the dates of the earliest reports of large-scale VL outbreaks in the ISC (Gibson, 1983) and thus suggesting that modern lowland parasites descend from these early epidemics.
evidence: This is an inference based on the phylogenetic dating and historical records.

claim: Within the core population, the Indo-Nepalese population itself appeared around 1900, almost certainly in India.
source: Within the core population, the Indo-Nepalese population itself appeared around 1900 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), almost certainly in India (0.89 posterior probability), matching the dates of the first reported outbreaks in Bihar (Gibson, 1983), more precisely in Purnea (Figure 2d).
evidence: This is a result from the phylogeographic analysis.

claim: Most subsequent diversification is more recent, with many groups (ISC2 & ISC4-6) radiating from the 1960s, coinciding with the end of the DDT spraying campaign.
source: Most subsequent diversification is more recent, with many groups (ISC2 & ISC4-6) radiating from the 1960s (Figure 1b), coinciding with the end of the DDT spraying campaign.
evidence: This is a result from the phylogenetic dating analysis.

claim: The estimated rate of migration from India to Nepal in the Core 191 group was significantly greater than that from Nepal to India.
source: The estimated rate of migration from India to Nepal in the Core 191 group was significantly greater than that from Nepal to India, suggesting that India acts as a source population seeding the Nepalese epidemic (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result from the phylogeographic analysis.

claim: India acts as a source population seeding the Nepalese epidemic.
source: The estimated rate of migration from India to Nepal in the Core 191 group was significantly greater than that from Nepal to India, suggesting that India acts as a source population seeding the Nepalese epidemic (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an inference based on the migration rate estimates.

claim: A lack of linkage disequilibrium decay between SNP pairs with genomic distance in the core population reflects a lack of detectable recombination within the six main genetic groups.
source: A lack of linkage disequilibrium decay between SNP pairs with genomic distance in the core population (r2~0.33 at 5–1,400 kb) reflects a lack of detectable recombination within the six main genetic groups (ISC2-7) across the entire genome (Supplementary file 2, table j).
evidence: This is a result from the linkage disequilibrium analysis.

claim: There is compelling evidence of hybridisation among eight of the samples not assigned to any of the ISC groups.
source: While the low number of SNPs varying within the core population limits our power to detect recombination, we find compelling evidence of hybridisation among eight of the samples not assigned to any of the ISC groups (Figure 2—figure supplements 2–4).
evidence: This is a finding from the haplotype analysis.

claim: The four-allele test confirms that recombination is largely restricted to hybrid isolates.
source: The four-allele test also confirms that recombination is largely restricted to these hybrids (Supplementary file 2, table o).
evidence: This is a result from a statistical test for recombination.

claim: Eight isolates appear to result from multiple independent recent hybridizations between distinct ancestors of either ISC5 and ISC6, ISC5 and ISC7, or ISC6 and ISC7.
source: These isolates appear to result from multiple independent recent hybridizations between distinct ancestors of either ISC5 and ISC6, ISC5 and ISC7, or ISC6 and ISC7 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an inference about the origin of hybrid isolates based on haplotype analysis.

claim: Local copy-number variants (CNVs) cover ~11% of the genome.
source: We detect extensive variation in the structure of these L. donovani genomes. Local copy-number variants (CNVs) cover ~11% of the genome.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the structural variant analysis.

claim: Two multigenic intra-chromosomal duplicated regions (MAPK1 and H-locus) are present in variable numbers in all core population isolates but are absent in ISC1.
source: Two multigenic intra-chromosomal duplicated regions (MAPK1 and H-locus; Downing et al., 2011) are present in variable numbers in all core population isolates but are absent in ISC1 (Figure 3b,c; Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the copy number analysis.

claim: Conserved heterozygous SNPs in both MAPK1 and H-locus duplicated regions confirm that these regions have duplicated once and been maintained throughout the evolution of this population.
source: Conserved heterozygous SNPs in both of these structural variants confirm that these regions have duplicated once and been maintained throughout the evolution of this population.
evidence: This is an inference about the evolutionary history of these duplications based on SNP patterns.

claim: All known genes on the MAPK1 and H-locus duplicated regions are associated with virulence or drug resistance.
source: All known genes on these duplicated regions are associated with virulence (MAPK1, ASS, sAcP; Fernandes et al., 2013; Lakhal-Naouar et al., 2012; Wiese, 1998) or drug resistance (Brotherton et al., 2013), indicating that extensive structural variation allows these parasites to alter local copy number in response to changing environments: both aneuploidy and CNV regulate gene expression (Leprohon et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a statement about the functional significance of genes in duplicated regions, supported by citations.

claim: Extensive structural variation allows these parasites to alter local copy number in response to changing environments.
source: All known genes on these duplicated regions are associated with virulence (MAPK1, ASS, sAcP; Fernandes et al., 2013; Lakhal-Naouar et al., 2012; Wiese, 1998) or drug resistance (Brotherton et al., 2013), indicating that extensive structural variation allows these parasites to alter local copy number in response to changing environments: both aneuploidy and CNV regulate gene expression (Leprohon et al., 2009).
evidence: This is an inference about the adaptive significance of structural variation.

claim: Both aneuploidy and CNV regulate gene expression.
source: All known genes on these duplicated regions are associated with virulence (MAPK1, ASS, sAcP; Fernandes et al., 2013; Lakhal-Naouar et al., 2012; Wiese, 1998) or drug resistance (Brotherton et al., 2013), indicating that extensive structural variation allows these parasites to alter local copy number in response to changing environments: both aneuploidy and CNV regulate gene expression (Leprohon et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a cited observation about the functional consequences of structural variation.

claim: Most isolates are aneuploid, even excluding the generally tetrasomic chromosome 31.
source: Most isolates are aneuploid (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), even excluding the generally tetrasomic chromosome 31, and almost all chromosomes show some variation in somy (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is a finding from the somy analysis.

claim: Almost all chromosomes show some variation in somy.
source: Most isolates are aneuploid (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), even excluding the generally tetrasomic chromosome 31, and almost all chromosomes show some variation in somy (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is a finding from the somy analysis.

claim: Aneuploidy is significantly correlated with SNP variation in the core isolates.
source: Aneuploidy (r2=0.15, p=2.7x10-118), CNVs (r2=0.26, p=7.5x10-218) and indels (r2=0.30, p=2.1x10-254) are significantly correlated with SNP variation in the core isolates, suggesting that these variants have appeared gradually during the evolution of the population in the field.
evidence: This is a statistical result showing correlation between different types of genetic variation.

claim: CNVs are significantly correlated with SNP variation in the core isolates.
source: Aneuploidy (r2=0.15, p=2.7x10-118), CNVs (r2=0.26, p=7.5x10-218) and indels (r2=0.30, p=2.1x10-254) are significantly correlated with SNP variation in the core isolates, suggesting that these variants have appeared gradually during the evolution of the population in the field.
evidence: This is a statistical result showing correlation between different types of genetic variation.

claim: Indels are significantly correlated with SNP variation in the core isolates.
source: Aneuploidy (r2=0.15, p=2.7x10-118), CNVs (r2=0.26, p=7.5x10-218) and indels (r2=0.30, p=2.1x10-254) are significantly correlated with SNP variation in the core isolates, suggesting that these variants have appeared gradually during the evolution of the population in the field.
evidence: This is a statistical result showing correlation between different types of genetic variation.

claim: Structural variants have appeared gradually during the evolution of the population in the field.
source: Aneuploidy (r2=0.15, p=2.7x10-118), CNVs (r2=0.26, p=7.5x10-218) and indels (r2=0.30, p=2.1x10-254) are significantly correlated with SNP variation in the core isolates, suggesting that these variants have appeared gradually during the evolution of the population in the field.
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between structural variants and SNPs.

claim: Two cases of recent epidemic expansions are associated with major changes in aneuploidy and heterozygosity.
source: Most strikingly, we find two cases of recent epidemic expansions associated with major changes in aneuploidy and heterozygosity (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of somy and heterozygosity patterns.

claim: Variation in somy can lead to changes in heterozygosity, which could allow selection to eradicate recessive deleterious mutations in the absence of recombination.
source: Variation in somy can thus lead to changes in heterozygosity, which could allow selection to eradicate recessive deleterious mutations in the absence of recombination (Roze and Michod, 2010).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the evolutionary consequences of somy variation, supported by a citation.

claim: No statistically significant association was found between any individual SNP or structural genetic variant and in vitro SSG resistance.
source: We find no statistically significant association between any individual SNP or structural genetic variant and in vitro SSG resistance, or SSG or MIL treatment outcomes (Supplementary file 2, tables p–r), but the distribution of antimony susceptibility was uneven across different ISC populations (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a negative result from the association analysis.

claim: The distribution of antimony susceptibility was uneven across different ISC populations.
source: We find no statistically significant association between any individual SNP or structural genetic variant and in vitro SSG resistance, or SSG or MIL treatment outcomes (Supplementary file 2, tables p–r), but the distribution of antimony susceptibility was uneven across different ISC populations (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is an observation about the distribution of drug resistance phenotypes.

claim: 9 of 11 ISC5 samples tested were highly SbV-resistant.
source: 9 of 11 ISC5 samples tested were highly SbV-resistant and two out of four ISC5-ISC6/7 hybrids tested have intermediate levels of resistance.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the drug susceptibility testing.

claim: Two out of four ISC5-ISC6/7 hybrids tested have intermediate levels of resistance.
source: 9 of 11 ISC5 samples tested were highly SbV-resistant and two out of four ISC5-ISC6/7 hybrids tested have intermediate levels of resistance.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the drug susceptibility testing.

claim: A two-bp insertion introducing a frameshift and premature stop codon in the aquaglyceroporin-1 gene (AQP1) is homozygous in all 52 ISC5 isolates.
source: One variant – a two-bp insertion introducing a frameshift and premature stop codon in the aquaglyceroporin-1 gene (LdBPK_310030, AQP1) – is homozygous in all 52 ISC5 isolates (Table 1), and heterozygous in six hybrids between ISC5 and either ISC6 or ISC7.
evidence: This is a key finding linking a specific genetic variant to the ISC5 population.

claim: The AQP1 frameshift is heterozygous in six hybrids between ISC5 and either ISC6 or ISC7.
source: One variant – a two-bp insertion introducing a frameshift and premature stop codon in the aquaglyceroporin-1 gene (LdBPK_310030, AQP1) – is homozygous in all 52 ISC5 isolates (Table 1), and heterozygous in six hybrids between ISC5 and either ISC6 or ISC7.
evidence: This is a finding about the distribution of the AQP1 variant in hybrid isolates.

claim: ISC5 isolates have higher copy number of both the H-locus and MAPK1 amplicons.
source: ISC5 isolates also share other genomic features – such as higher copy number of both the H-locus and MAPK1 amplicons (Figure 3b,c).
evidence: This is a finding from the copy number analysis.

claim: The H-locus includes MRPA, a gene involved in the efflux of SbIII and associated with drug resistance.
source: The H-locus includes MRPA, a gene involved in the efflux of SbIII and associated with drug resistance (Leprohon et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a cited statement about the function of a gene in the H-locus.

claim: AQP1 is known to assist with SbIII uptake.
source: Other lines of evidence strongly link AQP1 with antimony resistance. While recent antimonial drugs such as SSG are compounds of pentavalent antimony (SbV), SbV is thought to act mostly as a pro-drug, being reduced to SbIII in both the macrophage phagolysosome (Frézard et al., 2001) and in the parasite itself (Denton et al., 2004; Decuypere et al., 2012). AQP1 is known to assist with SbIII uptake, both genetic and transcriptional changes at this locus have been associated with Sb resistance (Gourbal et al., 2004; Monte-Neto et al., 2015; Mukherjee et al., 2013; Uzcategui et al., 2008) and a homologous transporter is associated with drug resistance in trypanosomes (Baker et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a cited statement about the function of AQP1.

claim: Both genetic and transcriptional changes at the AQP1 locus have been associated with Sb resistance.
source: Other lines of evidence strongly link AQP1 with antimony resistance. While recent antimonial drugs such as SSG are compounds of pentavalent antimony (SbV), SbV is thought to act mostly as a pro-drug, being reduced to SbIII in both the macrophage phagolysosome (Frézard et al., 2001) and in the parasite itself (Denton et al., 2004; Decuypere et al., 2012). AQP1 is known to assist with SbIII uptake, both genetic and transcriptional changes at this locus have been associated with Sb resistance (Gourbal et al., 2004; Monte-Neto et al., 2015; Mukherjee et al., 2013; Uzcategui et al., 2008) and a homologous transporter is associated with drug resistance in trypanosomes (Baker et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a cited statement about the role of AQP1 in drug resistance.

claim: A homologous transporter to AQP1 is associated with drug resistance in trypanosomes.
source: Other lines of evidence strongly link AQP1 with antimony resistance. While recent antimonial drugs such as SSG are compounds of pentavalent antimony (SbV), SbV is thought to act mostly as a pro-drug, being reduced to SbIII in both the macrophage phagolysosome (Frézard et al., 2001) and in the parasite itself (Denton et al., 2004; Decuypere et al., 2012). AQP1 is known to assist with SbIII uptake, both genetic and transcriptional changes at this locus have been associated with Sb resistance (Gourbal et al., 2004; Monte-Neto et al., 2015; Mukherjee et al., 2013; Uzcategui et al., 2008) and a homologous transporter is associated with drug resistance in trypanosomes (Baker et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a cited statement about drug resistance in related organisms.

claim: An AQP1 knockout line of Leishmania major was shown to be resistant to SbIII due to reduced uptake.
source: Recently, an AQP1 knockout line of Leishmania major was shown to be resistant to SbIII due to reduced uptake (Plourde et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a cited experimental result supporting the role of AQP1 in antimony resistance.

claim: The truncated frameshift protein found in ISC5 is predicted to be incapable of forming a functional trans-membrane channel.
source: The truncated frameshift protein found in ISC5 is predicted to be incapable of forming a functional trans-membrane channel (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is a prediction based on protein modeling.

claim: Three other independent frameshifts in AQP1 gene were found in other antimony resistant isolates.
source: We find three other independent frameshifts in AQP1 gene in other antimony resistant isolates, including one in BPK181/12 (ISC6), an isolate taken from a patient following failure of ten months of antimony treatment that was absent in the pre-treatment isolate from the same patient (BPK181/ 0cl11, Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding showing multiple independent mutations in AQP1 associated with resistance.

claim: One AQP1 frameshift was found in BPK181/12 (ISC6), an isolate taken from a patient following failure of ten months of antimony treatment that was absent in the pre-treatment isolate from the same patient.
source: We find three other independent frameshifts in AQP1 gene in other antimony resistant isolates, including one in BPK181/12 (ISC6), an isolate taken from a patient following failure of ten months of antimony treatment that was absent in the pre-treatment isolate from the same patient (BPK181/ 0cl11, Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding showing the emergence of an AQP1 mutation during treatment.

claim: The AQP1 truncation is associated with antimonial resistance in the ancestor of ISC5.
source: We propose that the AQP1 truncation is associated with antimonial resistance in the ancestor of ISC5, and has been transmitted to a group of hybrid parasites.
evidence: This is a proposed hypothesis based on the genetic and phenotypic data.

claim: The AQP1 truncation has been transmitted to a group of hybrid parasites.
source: We propose that the AQP1 truncation is associated with antimonial resistance in the ancestor of ISC5, and has been transmitted to a group of hybrid parasites.
evidence: This is a proposed hypothesis based on the genetic data showing the variant in hybrids.

claim: The ISC5 lineage emerged following the end of the DDT campaigns but then proliferated quickly in the 1970s.
source: The ISC5 lineage emerged following the end of the DDT campaigns but then proliferated quickly in the 1970s (Figure 1c,d), when antimonial dosage had to be doubled because of its declining efficacy.
evidence: This is a result from the phylogenetic dating and population size analysis.

claim: Antimonial dosage had to be doubled in the 1970s because of its declining efficacy.
source: The ISC5 lineage emerged following the end of the DDT campaigns but then proliferated quickly in the 1970s (Figure 1c,d), when antimonial dosage had to be doubled because of its declining efficacy.
evidence: This is a historical observation about drug treatment practices.

claim: The persistence of the ISC5 lineage beyond the era of Sb treatment perhaps reflects the increased fitness of Sb-resistant parasites.
source: The persistence of this lineage beyond the era of Sb treatment perhaps reflects the increased fitness (Vanaerschot et al., 2013) of Sb-resistant parasites.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the evolutionary dynamics of the resistant population.

claim: ISC5 shows a stronger signature of purifying selection compared to other ISC populations.

claim: Two resistant strains from ISC4 (BPK087 and BPK190) show significantly decreased transcription of an AQP1 locus encoding a wildtype protein sequence.
source: Indeed, other SbV resistance mechanisms are known in this population: previous work has shown that two resistant strains from ISC4 (BPK087 and BPK190) show significantly decreased transcription of an AQP1 locus encoding a wildtype protein sequence (Decuypere et al., 2005), and BHU764 combines a different indel mutation in AQP1 and reduced expression of MRPA, an efflux transporter of SbIII (Mukhopadhyay et al., 2011).

claim: Genomic data can retrospectively unravel the evolution and epidemiology of this parasite population.
source: We have shown that genomic data can retrospectively unravel the evolution and epidemiology of this parasite population, and gain new insight into possible mechanisms of drug resistance against a background of extensive variation in genome structure.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the capabilities demonstrated in the study.

claim: This is the first analysis of the structure and history of a Leishmania population, aligned with clinical and epidemiological records.
source: We report the first analysis of the structure and history of a Leishmania population, aligned with clinical and epidemiological records, enabled by the higher resolution of genome sequence data than other genotyping approaches.

claim: Continued genetic surveillance of parasite populations is key to rapidly identify and respond to the emergence of treatment failure.
source: Continued genetic surveillance of parasite populations is key to rapidly identify and respond to the emergence of treatment failure.

claim: Genomic data has led to the identification of the major locus underlying artemisinin resistance in Plasmodium falciparum.
source: In the recent emergence of artemisinin resistance in Plasmodium falciparum, genomic data has led to the identification of the major locus underlying resistance (Ariey et al., 2014; Cheeseman et al., 2012), revealed the genetic architecture of resistance (Miotto et al., 2015) and shed light on the population genetic context in which resistance is appearing (Miotto et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a cited example of genomic surveillance in another parasite.

claim: Miltefosine has shown reduced efficacy in both India and Nepal.

evidence: This is a cited observation about current drug efficacy.

claim: Amphotericin B is now being used against visceral leishmaniasis in ISC.

claim: SbV is thought to act mostly as a pro-drug, being reduced to SbIII in both the macrophage phagolysosome and in the parasite itself.
source: While recent antimonial drugs such as SSG are compounds of pentavalent antimony (SbV), SbV is thought to act mostly as a pro-drug, being reduced to SbIII in both the macrophage phagolysosome (Frézard et al., 2001) and in the parasite itself (Denton et al., 2004; Decuypere et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a cited statement about the mechanism of action of antimonial drugs.
